LanguageData.LP_LichScenario.label: the phylactery is formed
LanguageData.LP_LichScenario.description:
Your master died of plague and your fellow students were burned by witch-hunting paladins. You fled with the master's notes into an ancient crypt beneath the wastes and lived there alone for many years. You practiced on the corpses of beasts and grave robbers, stitched together two skeletons, and piled up three seasons of raw meat into a flesh golem. Tonight, alone in the crypt, you completed the final step of the ritual and sealed both heart and soul into the phylactery. No living soul is in the crypt; only these necromantic constructs guard the door. The sun went dark the moment the ritual was complete.

You start with a single character, who becomes the lich (a psychically deaf one is still converted, but phylactery spells and repair will be weak, so reroll). Liches don't eat or sleep but need raw meat and intact corpses to feed the phylactery. The Thayan expedition has heard of your ritual and treats you as a fellow traveler for now: starting goodwill 0, kept there for 60 days by "old covenant", then gradually dropping unless you swear allegiance to the Red Wizards.

Note: no living companions; early manpower relies entirely on necromantic constructs; a challenging start.

LanguageData.LP_LichScenario.scenario.name: the phylactery is formed
LanguageData.LP_LichScenario.scenario.parts.GameStart:
As the last incantation fell, your heart stopped, yet you did not die.

Your soul sank into that cold phylactery, and the skeletons and flesh golem in the crypt opened their hollow eyes together, awaiting your orders. For years they have been your only companions; from tonight, like them, you no longer need to eat or sleep. No heart beats in the crypt anymore.

Outside, the sun has been swallowed by shadow.

Protect the phylactery. As long as it remains, death is only a three-day sleep.
LanguageData.LP_LichScenario.scenario.summary: A lich who just completed the ritual with no living companions; a phylactery, ritual table and three necromantic constructs.
LanguageData.LP_FireGiantScenario.label: forge exiles
LanguageData.LP_FireGiantScenario.description:
A volcanic eruption swallowed your clan's forge hall. Three fire giants escaped carrying embers from the forge that hadn't yet gone out, and relit the forge in this strange land. Volcanic ash blots out the sky, and the cold is what fire giants fear most.

(The molten forge and smith's coat have been removed since 1.146.0.)

Note: fire giants are slow and fear the cold; the volcanic winter of the first few days makes staying warm the top priority.

LanguageData.LP_FireGiantScenario.scenario.name: forge exiles
LanguageData.LP_FireGiantScenario.scenario.parts.Game:
The night the volcano woke, the dome of the forge hall collapsed.

The three of you carried the last red-hot coal from the forge's heart in iron tongs, walking all the way to where ash had turned the sky the color of lead.

The land here is strange and cold. First get the forge roaring again, then make this land remember the sound of fire giant hammers.
LanguageData.LP_FireGiantScenario.scenario.summary: Three fire giants. Fear the cold; challenging.
LanguageData.LP_TrollScenario.label: tribe in the ashes
LanguageData.LP_TrollScenario.description:
Torch-bearing hunters burned your camp. Only the bodies that escaped the flames knit back together at dawn the next day and crawled up. Four hungry trolls, with two worgs, left their smoking homeland.

Tribal tech start. Trolls regenerate fast when fed and revive after death unless burned; they've just grown back from death, so their bodies are still weak and their stomachs empty. The Thayan expedition once hired your tribe: starting goodwill 0, kept there for 60 days by "old covenant", then gradually dropping to hostile.

Note: trolls eat a lot, and you start with only raw meat and a little pemmican, so hunt as soon as possible.

LanguageData.LP_TrollScenario.scenario.name: tribe in the ashes
LanguageData.LP_TrollScenario.scenario.parts.GameStar:
They came at night with torches.

Your kin fell one after another, and the hunters burned every body they could find. But they didn't find everyone.

At dawn the next day you knit back together in the mud, torn wounds slowly closing, your empty stomach roaring. Three companions stood up too, and two worgs followed the scent out of the woods back to you.

Leave the smoking homeland. Go find meat, and a place without fire.
LanguageData.LP_TrollScenario.scenario.summary: Four trolls just grown back from death and two worgs, tribal tech.
LanguageData.LP_HalfOrcScenario.label: brokenchain warband
LanguageData.LP_HalfOrcScenario.description:
You were orc slave soldiers under Thay's Red Wizards, slave brands on your foreheads, digging trenches, carrying shields and dying at the front for the expedition. One night of rout, four half-orcs smashed their leg irons, grabbed weapons and fled into the wilds. The Red Wizards never let runaway slaves go.

Tribal tech start; all four are "brokenchain exiles", each with a steel mace or spear. Goodwill with the Thayan expedition is -100 (just the starting value; it can be eased as usual afterwards); Faerûn's pioneer league sympathizes with runaway slaves, goodwill +20. Around day 6, "the Red Wizards' pursuers" make a small raid (about 0.6× vanilla threat), and after that it's up to you.

Note: there's a destined pursuer fight right at the start, but half-orcs are tough and can hold on a bit longer before falling; medium difficulty.

LanguageData.LP_HalfOrcScenario.scenario.name: brokenchain warband
LanguageData.LP_HalfOrcScenario.scenario.parts.GameSt:
The sound of chains breaking was louder than any war drum.

The four of you stormed out of the camp over the guards' bodies and ran until dawn, until you could no longer hear the Red Wizards' horns. You grip looted maces and spears, with half a shackle still hanging from your ankles.

The Red Wizards never let runaway slaves go. Before the pursuers arrive, find somewhere you can hold.
LanguageData.LP_HalfOrcScenario.scenario.summary: Four half-orc runaway slaves who smashed their leg irons, tribal tech; on day 6 the Red Wizards' pursuers arrive.
LanguageData.LP_ElfScenario.label: moonlit woodland
LanguageData.LP_ElfScenario.description:
Three elven rangers left a declining woodland court and followed the moonlight to this empty woodland. The Harpers of Faerûn's pioneer league are their old friends and gather news for them along the way.

The best archer among the elves has a level 1 psylink: elves enter "meditative breath" while sleeping, and psychically gifted elves regain about 20% psyfocus each night. Goodwill with Faerûn's pioneer league is +65, meeting the Harper warning threshold (≥60) from the start: big raids are delayed 1-2 days and announced in advance by letter. A forest or temperate forest start is recommended (the scenario doesn't force a biome).

Note: only three people, bows as the only weapons, an industrial start but with few supplies; medium difficulty.

LanguageData.LP_ElfScenario.scenario.name: moonlit woodland
LanguageData.LP_ElfScenario.scenario.parts.GameStartD:
Moonlight leaks through the gaps in the canopy onto your bowstrings.

The woodland court is empty now, and only the three of you still remember the ancient songs. A secret letter from the Harpers says this woodland has no owner.

Plant that seed. When it grows into a great tree, this will be the new court.
LanguageData.LP_ElfScenario.scenario.summary: Three elven rangers, a longbow and a Pholx seed; the Harpers are on your side from the start.
LanguageData.LP_DwarfScenario.label: oath of the deep mountain
LanguageData.LP_DwarfScenario.description:
Three dwarves swore an oath before their ancestors' stele: to carve a fortress beneath new mountains, and to make the ember clan pay for the mines they burned long ago. They crossed the mountains carrying beer barrels and steel ingots.

The starting supplies (beer, steel, plasteel, granite blocks, a steel hammer and a steel plate armor) are placed in a nearby cave with a thick rock roof, the "mountain camp"; dwarves get mood +3 under thick rock roofs and mine and work faster (stone endurance). The best miner also has a minor passion for Crafting. Goodwill with Faerûn's pioneer league is +50, with the ember clan -60 (sworn enemies). If no mountain can be found nearby, the supplies are placed normally and a letter lets you know, so a hills or mountains start is recommended.

Note: few people but solid gear, moderate difficulty; a flat start loses most of the benefit of stone endurance.

LanguageData.LP_DwarfScenario.scenario.name: oath of the deep mountain
LanguageData.LP_DwarfScenario.scenario.parts.GameStar:
"By stone as witness, by fire as oath."

The three of you set down your packs at the foot of the mountain and nail a rubbing of the ancestors' stele to the rock wall. The cave is dry, the beer barrels neatly stacked.

Carve open this mountain. Once the fortress gate stands, go settle the score with the ember clan.
LanguageData.LP_DwarfScenario.scenario.summary: Three oath-sworn dwarves with supplies stored in a nearby cave; sworn enemies of the ember clan.
LanguageData.LP_MindFlayerScenario.label: escape from the colony
LanguageData.LP_MindFlayerScenario.description:
A mind flayer heard a stray noise in the elder brain's whispers, and then it could no longer hear the elder brain at all. It fled the Underdark colony with a half-transformed human servant, dragging along two captives meant to feed the elder brain. The colony doesn't tolerate defectors.

The mind flayer starts with 60 brain matter, and the two bound human prisoners are its first brain matter source (the bonds loosen after about 5 days; build a prison cell quickly). The human colonist has a tadpole at 30% progress in the brain and is under a psionic suppressant: a "half-illithid" who keeps their self; the 3 suppressants carried must be used sparingly, since 3 days without the pills resumes ceremorphosis. There are 2 more tadpoles. Around days 10-15, the Underdark colony's pursuers burst out of the ground. With a mind flayer in the colony, Faerûn's pioneer league naturally drops -25 goodwill from racial opinion, and witch-hunting zealots may show up early too.

Note: few people, many enemies, and food comes from brains; a hard start.

LanguageData.LP_MindFlayerScenario.scenario.name: escape from the colony
LanguageData.LP_MindFlayerScenario.scenario.parts.Con: A mind flayer and a human servant.
LanguageData.LP_MindFlayerScenario.scenario.parts.Gam:
The voice of the elder brain is gone.

First came dizziness, then a silence you'd never known; for the first time you heard your own thoughts. You crawled out from underground dragging your servant and two captives, the sunlight stinging your tentacles.

The colony will send someone to find you. Before then, eat your fill, then get ready.
LanguageData.LP_MindFlayerScenario.scenario.summary: A defecting mind flayer, a half-illithid servant and two captives; the colony's pursuers will burst out of the ground.
LanguageData.LP_MinotaurScenario.label: lords of the labyrinth
LanguageData.LP_MinotaurScenario.description:
Two minotaurs deserted the shock troops of the Thayan expedition, along with a half-orc deserter. In the wilds they found an ancient stone-walled labyrinth, and once the minotaurs walked in they never wanted to leave.

Near the start is a roughly 17×17 granite labyrinth ruin, fully roofed with only one entrance; the 5×5 central room holds two bedrolls, pemmican and herbal medicine. Minotaurs have a natural sense of direction and are in their element in the labyrinth. The minotaurs and the half-orc like each other (mood +2 each). Goodwill with the Thayan expedition is -100. If no flat ground can be found nearby, the labyrinth isn't generated and a letter explains why.

Note: the labyrinth is easy to defend but hard to expand; the Red Wizards show deserters no mercy; medium difficulty.

LanguageData.LP_MinotaurScenario.scenario.name: lords of the labyrinth
LanguageData.LP_MinotaurScenario.scenario.parts.GameS:
Moss covers the stone walls, and the passages are so narrow only one person can pass.

Others would get lost here, but you can reach the center with your eyes closed. The half-orc deserter grumbles along behind, but even he admits: this is the hardest place for the Red Wizards to find.

Hold the entrance. Let the pursuers wander the walls until dark.
LanguageData.LP_MinotaurScenario.scenario.summary: Two minotaurs and a half-orc deserter, holding an ancient stone-walled labyrinth.
LanguageData.LP_GithyankiScenario.label: silver sword squad
LanguageData.LP_GithyankiScenario.description:
Three githyanki astral warriors hunting mind flayers got lost on this strange planet. A stranded lich took them in; the githyanki have served the undying lich-queen for generations, and they won't forget this kindness. Now the lich sleeps in a distant crypt, and the squad has to find a foothold here for themselves.

The best melee warrior carries a silver longsword of excellent quality, the other two steel longswords; all wear steel plate armor and have a level 1 psylink. Goodwill with Faerûn's pioneer league is 0; the Underdark colony is a sworn enemy as always, and around day 8 "tentacles squirm underground": colony raiders will burst out of the ground.

Note: strong in combat, few hands, lacking production skills; medium difficulty.

LanguageData.LP_GithyankiScenario.scenario.name: silver sword squad
LanguageData.LP_GithyankiScenario.scenario.parts.Game:
The silver light of the Astral Plane closes behind you.

You followed the mind flayers' trail jump after jump, and finally landed on this strange land. The lich's kindness isn't yet repaid, and the smell of tentacles is already spreading underground.

Draw your silver swords. This time, the prey will come to you.
LanguageData.LP_GithyankiScenario.scenario.summary: Three githyanki astral warriors and a silver longsword; on day 8 the Underdark colony will burst out of the ground.
LanguageData.LP_NetherilHeirScenario.label: Netherese heir
LanguageData.LP_NetherilHeirScenario.description:
Beneath a fallen Netherese flying city, a human wizard found study scrolls left by his teacher in the rubble. He can already feel the Scroll of Karsus whispering from afar, and Larloch the Shadow King has sensed him too. Two companions left the ruins with him.

Recommended path: arcane ascension. Difficulty: medium.

The first person on the starting pawn page is the wizard: psylink level 4 (psycaster level 8 with Vanilla Psycasts Expanded), Intellectual at least 10, already carrying 2 stacks of "echo of Karsus". The "Netherese arcana" and "theurgy" research are complete. You start with two excellent-quality Netherese study scrolls, one arcane fragment, and the gold and mithril needed to build a Netherese altar. Goodwill with the retinue of Larloch the Shadow King is 0; on day 10 Larloch's envoy is sure to arrive, bringing "Larloch's invitation".

Note: only three people, with a wizard as the core; every deal with Larloch has a price.

LanguageData.LP_NetherilHeirScenario.scenario.name: Netherese heir
LanguageData.LP_NetherilHeirScenario.scenario.parts.C: Three humans; the first is a wizard.
LanguageData.LP_NetherilHeirScenario.scenario.parts.G:
The wreck of the flying city smokes behind you.

Your teacher's study scrolls still hold his warmth, and a name is hidden between the lines: Karsus. With every line you read, the echo in your mind grows clearer.

In a distant tomb, a pair of lidless eyes is reading you too. Within ten days, his envoy will come.
LanguageData.LP_NetherilHeirScenario.scenario.summary: A Netherese wizard and two companions; on day 10 the envoy of Larloch the Shadow King arrives. Recommended path: arcane ascension, difficulty medium.
LanguageData.LP_DoomLichScenario.label: doom approaches
LanguageData.LP_DoomLichScenario.description:
This lich has lived for three centuries, and its phylactery is nearly overflowing with souls. It has finally decided to take the one thing it hasn't yet: godhood. And Kelemvor, god of death, has finally decided it can't be allowed to live any longer.

Recommended path: demigod lich. Difficulty: hard.

The first character on the starting pawn page is the lich (if psychically deaf, whoever has the highest psychic sensitivity takes the role instead), with a level 20 phylactery commanding three skeleton servants and a necromantic ritual table nearby; another living apprentice handles eating and the things the dead can't do well. The demigod lich path is already open: trial one, "ten thousand souls", has drained 10 / 20 souls; Kelemvor's divine favor starts at -50. The "theurgy" research is complete. On day 5 Kelemvor's doomguards first send a small squad to destroy the phylactery (half the colony's threat points, not counting the trial's three waves).

Note: only two living people, the doomguards specialize in killing undead, and once the phylactery is destroyed this path is over.

LanguageData.LP_DoomLichScenario.scenario.name: doom approaches
LanguageData.LP_DoomLichScenario.scenario.parts.GameS:
The phylactery hums in your palm like a heart with too many heartbeats.

Every soul you've gathered in three hundred years whispers inside. Just one step more: drain ten more souls and you can reach for godhood.

But you hear the bell. It's the bell of death. His grey-robed guards are already on the way.
LanguageData.LP_DoomLichScenario.scenario.summary: A lich with a level 20 phylactery, an apprentice and three skeletons; on day 5 the doomguards come to destroy the phylactery. Recommended path: demigod lich, difficulty hard.
LanguageData.LP_PilgrimageScenario.label: the pilgrim's road
LanguageData.LP_PilgrimageScenario.description:
Three believers followed the same revelation for hundreds of miles: their god wants an altar raised on this land, and one of them is the god's own chosen one.

Recommended path: saint. Difficulty: medium.

The starting characters are all believers of the same god; the god is randomly chosen from the nine worshippable gods and follows the first person on the pawn page (rerolling the first person changes the god too), and the first person is that god's chosen one. This god is already the colony's patron deity, with 60 divine favor; the saint path is already open, stopped at trial one, "devotion". The "faith and divine magic" and "theurgy" research are complete. You start with a minified altar (select it and click "install"), a holy symbol and five miracle fragments.

Note: the saint path's bearing witness and the descent of holy fire both draw strong enemies; if divine favor drops below 60 you'll have to build it back up first.

LanguageData.LP_PilgrimageScenario.scenario.name: the pilgrim's road
LanguageData.LP_PilgrimageScenario.scenario.parts.Gam:
On the seventh night the revelation became clear: this is the place.

You unload the altar from the pack frame, and the holy symbol glows faintly on the chosen one's chest. The other two kneel to pray, their voices carried far by the wind.

The god is watching. First raise the altar, then let this land hear the god's name.
LanguageData.LP_PilgrimageScenario.scenario.summary: A chosen one and two believers of the same faith, carrying a minified altar. Recommended path: saint, difficulty medium.
LanguageData.LP_TwilightHunterScenario.label: twilight godhunters
LanguageData.LP_TwilightHunterScenario.description:
Four mercenaries had the same dream on the same night: the gods arguing under a dark red sky, and one god's spark slipping through its fingers. When the veteran leading them woke, his palm was still burning.

Recommended path: usurper. Difficulty: very hard.

The first person on the starting pawn page is the veteran: Shooting or Melee (whichever is higher) at least 12, psychic sensitivity at least 110% (swapped to the "psychically sensitive" trait if not enough). The Year of Twilight is sure to begin on day 3, lasting per settings. When a colonist defeats a god-possessed leader, the usurper path opens automatically. The "theurgy" research is complete. You start with five miracle fragments (+8% usurping ritual success each), a fine steel longsword and a fine assault rifle.

Note: during the Year of Twilight enemies are stronger and possessed leaders are extremely tough; a failed usurping ritual costs lives.
LanguageData.LP_TwilightHunterScenario.scenario.descr:
Four mercenaries had the same dream on the same night: the gods arguing under a dark red sky, and one god's spark slipping through its fingers. When the veteran leading them woke, his palm was still burning.

Recommended path: usurper. Difficulty: very hard.

The first person on the starting pawn page is the veteran: Shooting or Melee (whichever is higher) at least 12, psychic sensitivity at least 110% (swapped to the "psychically sensitive" trait if not enough). The Year of Twilight is sure to begin on day 3, lasting per settings. When a colonist defeats a god-possessed leader, the usurper path opens automatically. The "theurgy" research is complete. You start with five miracle fragments (+8% usurping ritual success each), a fine steel longsword and a fine assault rifle.

Note: during the Year of Twilight enemies are stronger and possessed leaders are extremely tough; a failed usurping ritual costs lives.
LanguageData.LP_TwilightHunterScenario.scenario.name: twilight godhunters
LanguageData.LP_TwilightHunterScenario.scenario.parts:
The horizon is already tinged dark red.

The veteran wipes his longsword and says nothing. The spark the god let slip in the dream still burns in his palm; in three days the gods will descend into mortal bodies, and then even gods can be killed.

Prepare the fragments, prepare the bullets. The Year of Twilight is coming.
LanguageData.LP_TwilightHunterScenario.scenario.summa: Four mercenaries and a dream of hunting gods; the Year of Twilight begins on day 3. Recommended path: usurper, difficulty very hard.
LanguageData.LP_AdventurerPartyScenario.label: adventuring party
LanguageData.LP_AdventurerPartyScenario.description:
A typical Faerûn adventuring party: a human, a high elf, a mountain dwarf, a lightfoot halfling and a half-orc. They took one last commission in a tavern, and the map the client left led them to this empty frontier.

Five people, five races: the elf and the dwarf can't stand each other at first (after 60 days they become old comrades), the halfling's luck and courage can save the day, and the half-orc can hold on for half a day before falling. Starting supplies are like the vanilla crashlanded start; good for players who want to try several common races at once.

Note: more people and more supplies; difficulty is about the same as the vanilla crashlanded start.

LanguageData.LP_AdventurerPartyScenario.scenario.part: One each: human, high elf, mountain dwarf, lightfoot halfling, half-orc.

The tavern keeper said this commission was "simple".

Now the five of you stand in a wasteland with no roads, no villages and no client. The elf complains about the dwarf's snoring, the dwarf complains about the elf's poetry, and the halfling is already looking for somewhere to start a cooking fire.

Since there's no going back, set up camp here.
